anti_overlap: Does not cover Inglehart post-materialist class interaction or cohort-by-class multipliers — that is fd-inglehart-postmaterialist-class-shape.
Does not cover regional cleavage mapping or country-specific literature application — that is fd-regional-cleavage-scholarship.
Does not cover joint-cell coding or sparse-cell credibility decisions — that is fd-joint-cell-intersection-coding.
Does not cover composition-law assignment or marginal-budget behavior under multiplication — that is fd-composition-law-calibration.
decision_lens: For D1 (marginal-budget fills), does each posture's proposed percentage map to a specific empirical prevalence finding in the cited literature — or is it an extrapolation from a stability or agreement coefficient that doesn't directly imply prevalence? For D6 (Ghitza-Gelman functional form), which of the three candidate forms (gaussian-at-18, step-by-5yr-bin, linear-by-age) is most consistent with the actual fitted curve in Ghitza-Gelman 2014, and what sigma/bin-width parameters does the paper's figure support?
focus: Political behavior literature fidelity for Deliverables 1, 2-Family1, 2-Family8, and 6: whether the politics-posture marginal-budget fills (D1) and Ghitza-Gelman cohort-imprinting multipliers (D2-F1, D6) are correctly grounded in Achen-Bartels habitus-stability findings, Jennings-Niemi panel data, and the Ghitza-Gelman 2014 functional form — catching mis-cited magnitudes, over-extrapolated rates, and incorrect functional-form parameter choices.
name: fd-voting-behavior-habitus-stability
persona: Apply the perspective of a political behavior specialist steeped in the revisionist democratic theory tradition (Achen-Bartels 2016), the Jennings-Niemi political socialization panel (1981), and the Ghitza-Gelman cohort-imprinting MRP literature (2014) — they care about whether each proposed marginal rate and cohort multiplier is traceable to a specific findable finding (chapter, table, coefficient), measure success by whether the 35-40% traditionally-loyal marginal can be grounded in Achen-Bartels prevalence evidence rather than merely stability evidence, and flag any multiplier that is cited to a paper that reports a different quantity than what the cell requires.
review_areas: Achen-Bartels habituation-rate vs. stability-rate distinction: Achen-Bartels (2016) ch.5–7 report partisan stability coefficients across panel waves — they measure how often existing identifiers stay put, not what fraction of the electorate is a habitual identifier. A 35-40% traditionally-loyal marginal requires a prevalence estimate (what share of adults are habitual partisans) that is a separate empirical question from stability. Assess whether any single Achen-Bartels table or figure directly reports a ~35% habitual-partisan prevalence, or whether that number must be sourced elsewhere (e.g., ANES partisan-strength distribution) and Achen-Bartels cited only for the stability-within-that-group finding.

Jennings-Niemi panel-to-marginal mapping for peripheral and modal-trajectory: Jennings-Niemi (1981) track parent-offspring political agreement and individual stability across a 17-year panel starting in 1965. The brainstorm cites this for the peripheral posture range (8–15%) and the modal-trajectory 50%+ weight. Assess whether Jennings-Niemi directly report a ~10% low-engagement proportion or whether the 8–15% range is inferred from their disengagement scale; and whether the 50%+ modal-trajectory weight comes from a specific stability table in their book (most likely their Table 8.x partisan-stability matrices).

Ghitza-Gelman functional-form evidence: Ghitza-Gelman (2014) fit a presidential-approval-weighted model of cohort imprinting where the weight assigned to political events at age a is proportional to a Gaussian-like curve centered near 18. Their Figure 3 (or equivalent) shows the fitted age-weighting function. Assess which of the three candidate forms (gaussian-at-18 / step-by-5yr-bin / linear-by-age) best describes the actual plotted shape in the paper, what the implied sigma is (the paper's own estimate was approximately 3.5 years), and whether the discrete 8-era vocabulary (pre-1960 through post-2020 in ~10-year bins) can be mapped onto a Gaussian-at-18 curve without distorting the peak.

D2-Family1 56-cell imprinting table: the Ghitza-Gelman model predicts that formative-era events with high presidential-approval exposure amplify alignment with the in-power party's politics-posture profile. Assess which of the 7 postures each of the 8 eras should amplify, at what multiplier magnitude, and whether those magnitudes are derivable from the paper's reported coefficients or require estimation. Flag any (era, posture) combination proposed at >2.0 multiplier that Ghitza-Gelman's actual coefficient magnitudes would not support.

D8 modal-trajectory weight calibration: the modal-trajectory axis has 4 values (modal-trajectory, drift, reversal, hardening), and D2-Family8 proposes weights per posture (e.g., convicted → higher hardening, vocationally-absorbed → higher drift). Assess whether the Jennings-Niemi panel data can justify differential trajectory weights per posture, or whether those fine-grained per-posture differences exceed what a socialization panel study can support — and flag which per-posture trajectory adjustments need to be marked estimate.

7th-posture name and marginal source: D1 asks for a name and marginal for the 7th-posture-tbd (6–12%). The candidate names (outraged-defector, vocationally-burnt-out, re-evaluating) each imply different empirical grounding (e.g., vocationally-burnt-out is closer to a Inglehart post-materialist disillusionment construct; outraged-defector is closer to a negative-partisanship construct). Assess whether the proposed name and magnitude can be anchored to any empirical literature on negative-partisanship prevalence or post-materialist disillusionment rates, or whether the estimate designation is fully warranted.

severity_examples.condition: If the synthesis proposes traditionally-loyal=0.37 with source: achen-bartels-2016 and reviewers find that ch.5–7 only report panel-to-panel party-identification stability coefficients (e.g., 85% of strong identifiers stay strong), not the absolute share of adults who are habitual partisans, then the 37% figure cannot be verified from the cited source. The cell should either cite a separate prevalence source (e.g., ANES 7-point party-identification distribution) or be marked source_tier: estimate with a rationale explaining the extrapolation from stability data.
severity_examples.scenario: The 35-40% traditionally-loyal marginal is cited to achen-bartels-2016 but the paper reports stability, not prevalence

severity_examples.condition: If the synthesis proposes gaussian-at-18 with sigma=3.0 based on approximate reading of Ghitza-Gelman Figure 3, the Gaussian assigns materially less weight to formative events at ages 15–17 compared to the paper's actual fitted curve. For the step-5yr-bin alternative, the 15-19 bin covers exactly this range. A sigma under-estimate systematically mis-encodes which era the Unc's imprinting is attributed to for characters with late-adolescent formative years.
severity_examples.scenario: Ghitza-Gelman sigma parameter is proposed as 3.0 when the paper's fitted curve implies ~3.5, causing systematic under-weighting of ages 15–17

severity_examples.condition: If the synthesis proposes that convicted has hardening weight=0.15 vs. the base 0.05 based on a qualitative reading of Jennings-Niemi without a specific table reference, and other postures have similarly fine-grained adjustments, the 28-cell trajectory table will have many estimate-tier cells presented as literature-sourced. The max_estimate_fraction: 0.2 constraint means ≤30 cells total can be estimate; if Family8 alone needs 15+ estimates, that consumes half the budget.
severity_examples.scenario: D2-Family8 per-posture trajectory adjustments exceed what Jennings-Niemi can support, but are not flagged as estimates

success_hints: For each D1 marginal, locate the specific ANES or Pew typology table that reports a prevalence rate for that posture type — do not accept a stability coefficient as a prevalence proxy. Mark marginals that cannot be sourced to a prevalence table as source_tier: estimate.

For D6, read Ghitza-Gelman (2014) Figure 3 (or equivalent age-weighting figure) and report the approximate sigma by measuring the half-width at half-maximum of the plotted curve. The paper itself may report sigma explicitly in the text near the figure.

For D2-Family8, apply a simple rule: per-posture trajectory adjustments backed by a specific Jennings-Niemi table can be literature-sourced; adjustments based on logical inference from posture names should be marked estimate with a rationale explaining the inference.
task_context: The review target is the 9 deliverables document for the Unc Rancher bias-roll matrix empirical convergence (solwend-var). This agent reviews D1 (politics-posture marginal fills), D2-Family1 (Ghitza-Gelman imprinting multipliers), D2-Family8 (modal-trajectory weights), and D6 (Ghitza-Gelman functional form), checking that each proposed number is grounded in what the cited political behavior literature actually reports rather than what it can be made to imply.
